body.claim: Sharks' ancestors were swimming before there were any trees.
body.why: The oldest shark relatives, known as spiny sharks, appeared around 439 million years ago. The earliest known trees, such as Wattieza, grew about 385 million years ago.

probes.question: Which appeared first: the oldest shark relatives (about 439 million years ago) or the earliest known trees (about 385 million years ago)?
True or false: the earliest known trees lived about 385 million years ago.

image_brief.show: A shark swimming in open water

claims.claim: The oldest shark relatives, known as spiny sharks, appeared around 439 million years ago
claims.quote: The oldest total-group chondrichthyans, known as acanthodians or "spiny sharks", appeared during the Early Silurian , around 439 million years ago.

claims.claim: The earliest known trees, such as Wattieza, grew about 385 million years ago
claims.quote: of fossils from the Middle Devonian about 385 million years ago united the crown of Wattieza to a root and trunk known since 1870

claims.claim: The Gilboa fossils (Wattieza) are described as the earliest known trees
claims.quote: These fossils have been described as the earliest known trees

claims.claim: Sharks' ancestors swam before there were trees; shark relatives appeared first (title, claim, probe p1 answer "Shark relatives")
claims.note: Verified by calculation: 439 million years ago is earlier than 385 million years ago (439 - 385 = 54 million years earlier).

claims.claim: Probe p2: the earliest known trees lived about 385 million years ago (true)
claims.quote: of fossils from the Middle Devonian about 385 million years ago united the crown of Wattieza to a root and trunk known since 1870
